manifest.title: Many Worlds Historian
manifest.tagline: Explore network history collected by Malcolm
manifest.description:
Many Worlds Historian is a web application for exploring network history collected by Malcolm.

* See activity over time, alerts, protocols and the busiest hosts for any time range.
* Click a host, protocol or rule to filter the whole page, and open any event to see its raw record.
* Access uses your Cloudron login.

This test version shows **simulated data only**. Everything on screen is invented, and the page says so in a banner.
manifest.changelog: * First test version, showing simulated Malcolm data.
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Sign in with your Cloudron account. Only users you grant access to this app can open it.

This version shows **simulated data**. It does not connect to a Malcolm instance yet.

manifest.title: Many Worlds Historian
manifest.tagline: Explore network history collected by Malcolm
manifest.description:
Many Worlds Historian is a web application for exploring network history collected by Malcolm.

* Opens on the report. The dashboard for exploring the history by hand is one click away.
* See activity over time, alerts, protocols and the busiest hosts for any time range.
* Click a host, protocol or rule to filter the whole page, and open any event to see its raw record.
* Open a printable report in three views: a one-page executive summary, an OT owner view and the full report.
* The report says whether the monitoring was complete, ranks findings by severity, and answers questions such as who sent commands to controllers, what changed, whether network zones are separated and who has remote access into the plant.
* Charts show the critical findings, when the hazard events happened, what the sensors recorded, the traffic between zones, the senders of controller commands and the hours AI model calls fall in.
* A chapter on AI agents grades every host from what can be seen on the wire: whether it talks to an AI model, whether it behaves like a program rather than a person, whether it then acts on the network, and whether that is concerning.
* Access uses your Cloudron login.

This test version shows **simulated data only**. Everything on screen is invented, and the page says so in a banner.
manifest.changelog:
* The app now opens on the report. The dashboard for exploring the history by hand is one click away.
* The report has a new chapter, Indicators of AI agent activity: twenty-two things that can be seen on the wire, grouped into contact with a model, rhythm, volume, what the host then did, hosts moving in step, and hidden traffic.
* Each host is assessed from which kinds of indicator it shows, not from a score: AI use, agent-like, acting, or concerning when it acts without approval, sits on the plant network, or sent a command to a controller.
* A new chart draws every host against every indicator, one cell per hit, so a group of hosts behaving identically is visible at a glance; each row also says its assessment in words.
* New findings: a host that calls a model and also drives machines over SSH or remote management, a host that uploads far more to a model service than it receives, and the same client fingerprint appearing on several hosts.
* Indicators that were looked for and not seen are listed as such, and so is anything Malcolm could not answer, with the reason. Nothing in the chapter reads the content of a conversation; it reads names, ports, fingerprints, sizes and times.
* The simulated plant now has upload-heavy agents, a retrieval store, remote management, an AI coding tool's own user agent, a model-weights download, DNS-over-HTTPS, a queue shared between agents, and an unregistered device calling a model with the same fingerprint as the others.
* The simulator can also run a whole client's plants at once: ten fictional Norwegian water plants, ready for a view across the fleet.
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Sign in with your Cloudron account. Only users you grant access to this app can open it.

This version shows **simulated data**. It does not connect to a Malcolm instance yet.

manifest.changelog:

The finding keeps its place in its own section and is marked "AI watch" there.
* New AI Risk item in the report's header jumps straight to the section, from any view.
* The watch adds no query and no measurement of its own; it says which hosts it can recognise and which rows it cannot, rather than implying the list is complete.
